issues.display_title: Issue #28: Fix Issue Sub Locations API Payload Missing City and State Data
issues.main_description_html:
Description

A data fetching issue was identified on the Backend API serving the Photographer Detail page.

When inspecting the "Sub Locations" modal on the frontend, the UI renders empty punctuation (,,) in the location column. Upon further investigation, the frontend is behaving this way because the backend payload for the sub_locations array is incomplete. The API is returning null or empty strings for specific regional data (like city or state/province), even though this data should be available for regions like Canada and the United States.

Root cause (confirmed in code)

The photographer detail action loads sublocations without preloading the City relation:

src/action/v1/photographers/getPhotographerDetailBySlug.go:46-47

var sublocations []models.DirectoryPhotographerSublocation
config.GetConnPhotographers().Where("photographer_id = ?", phot.ID).Find(&sublocations)

The model declares a foreign-key relation that GORM only populates when explicitly preloaded:

src/models/directory_photographer_sublocation.go

CityID int            `gorm:"column:city_id;not null" json:"city_id"`
City   *DirectoryCity `gorm:"foreignKey:CityID" json:"city"`   // <-- never loaded -> serializes as null

Because there is no .Preload("City"), every sublocation in the response has "city": null, so the frontend has no city / state-province name to render and falls back to ,,.

Fix

Preload the City relation (and, if state/province display requires it, the city's country/region) when fetching sublocations:

config.GetConnPhotographers().
    Preload("City").
    Where("photographer_id = ?", phot.ID).
    Find(&sublocations)

Notes for the assignee:

  • DirectoryCity currently exposes Name + CountryID (src/models/...city...go). Confirm where state/province comes from - if it's a separate column/relation (e.g. a region or via country_id), preload/return that too so the frontend gets both city and state.
  • The same missing-preload pattern may exist on other sublocation read paths - grep for DirectoryPhotographerSublocation reads and verify each.
  • The detail response is Redis-cached (PhotographerDetail); bump/invalidate the cache so the corrected payload is served.

Acceptance criteria

  • sub_locations[*].city is populated (not null) in the photographer detail payload when city_id resolves to a city.
  • City and state/province (and country, if shown) are present so the frontend location column renders correctly for Canada and US regions - no more ,,.
  • Sublocations with a missing/invalid city_id degrade gracefully (no 500).
  • Detail Redis cache invalidated so existing cached entries don't keep serving the incomplete payload.
  • Verified against the photographer in the report (Toronto, Canada - sublocations "Canada" / "United States").

RESULT

Confirmed root cause via direct DB check (read-only, joining photographer_sublocations -> city -> state/country): city.state_id is well-populated (e.g. Toronto sublocations resolve to Saskatchewan/Canada, Colorado/United States), but was never exposed by the model or query.

Changes (commit aeee603):

  • src/action/v1/photographers/getPhotographerDetailBySlug.go: sublocations query now does Preload("City.State").Preload("City.Country"), so sub_locations[*].city is populated with name, state, and country instead of null.
  • src/models/directory_city.go: added StateID/State *DirectoryState (foreign key city.state_id).
  • src/models/directory_state.go: this model previously mapped to a non-existent states table with mismatched columns (dead code, unused anywhere). Rewrote it to map to the real state table (id, name, country_id, state_code, type, latitude, longitude) and wired it into DirectoryCity.

Other DirectoryPhotographerSublocation read paths checked: getPhotographerLocation.go returns a flat SublocationInfo DTO that doesn't expose city/state at all (out of scope here); addSublocation/updateSublocation/removeSublocation already invalidate the detail cache on write.

Cache: existing PhotographerDetail Redis entries were cached before this fix and will keep serving the old (incomplete) payload until they expire (24h TTL) or are flushed manually - no code-level cache-version bump done since that constant is shared across many unrelated cache keys.

Build + existing test suite pass.

UPDATE

Follow-up commit c79fa1c: aligned sub_locations[*] shape with the old Node.js getPhotographersDetailBySlug response - now a flat object {id, name, addressLine1, addressLine2, cityId, cityName, country, continent, latitude, longitude} instead of raw model serialization. Dropped the city.state/DirectoryState model addition from the previous commit since the old Node response never exposed state/province (State confirmed unused).

RESULT

Status: PASSED

Issue #28 passed after the 2026-07-23 QA run. The live Photographer Detail API for alin-bugeag-iki6 now returns populated sublocation location data for Canada and the United States. The real photographer page also renders the Sub Locations entry point with Sub Locations (2) and receives the same populated sublocations payload from the server-rendered profile data. No executed real API check returned HTTP 500.

issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 11/06/26

✅ Implementation Complete — Ready for Unit Testing

Commit :
8abb560

Implementation :

Report

A photographer (Werner Getzmann) reports he can't edit or delete his branch (sub) locations.

  • gothru user id: 253
  • photographer username/slug: clever-click
  • Route: DELETE https://apil.gothru.co/photographers/profile/delete-sub-location/36
  • Status Code: 409 Conflict
  • Response body: 
    { "statusCode": 404, "data": { "messages": "Failed to delete sub-location" } }

🔒 The user's JWT was included in the report — omitted here on purpose (don't paste live auth tokens into issues). If it was shared anywhere public, it should be rotated/revoked.

Investigation notes (grounded in this repo)

1. The failing request is hitting the LEGACY API, not this Go service.

  • Reported path: /photographers/profile/delete-sub-location/36 on host apil.gothru.co.
  • This Go service's delete route is different: DELETE /v1/photographers/:identifier/sublocations/:sublocationId (src/routes/v1/photographersRoutes.go:54).
  • The reported response shape { "statusCode", "data": { "messages" } } is the legacy Node format. This Go service returns { "error": ... } via helpers.FormatResponse and never returns 409 (only 400 / 404 / 500 — see src/controllers/v1/sublocation/removeSublocation.go).
  • So first question for the assignee: is the dashboard still calling the legacy endpoint, and should it be migrated to the Go endpoint? Or is this a legacy-side bug? Confirm which backend owns delete-sublocation in production.

2. Likely cause in the Go delete path (if/when migrated).
RemoveSublocation (src/action/v1/sublocations/removeSublocation.go) deletes only when the row matches both id and owner:

db.Where("id = ? AND photographer_id = ?", sublocationID, photographer.ID).First(&sublocation) // -> ErrSublocationNotFound (404) if no match

The photographer is resolved from the :identifier (numeric → gothru_user_id, else → slug). If the dashboard passes an identifier that resolves to a photographer whose id ≠ the sublocation's photographer_id, this returns 404 "sublocation not found" — a plausible match for the reported 404 body. Verify that sublocation 36 actually belongs to the photographer with gothru_user_id = 253 / slug clever-click.

3. The 409 Conflict (HTTP) is suspicious.
A 409 at the HTTP layer (despite a 404 in the JSON body) typically indicates a database foreign-key constraint blocking the delete — i.e. other rows still reference photographer_sublocations.id = 36. Check for FK constraints / dependent rows before deleting, and delete/cascade them or return a clear error. (This 409 is almost certainly legacy-side, reinforcing note 1.)

Acceptance criteria

  • Confirm which backend serves delete-sublocation in production (legacy apil.gothru.co vs this Go service) and document it; if the dashboard should use the Go endpoint, track the migration.
  • Deleting sublocation 36 for gothru_user_id 253 / clever-click succeeds (or returns an accurate, actionable error if the row genuinely doesn't belong to that user).
  • If a FK/related-row constraint blocks deletion, it is handled (cascade or explicit, correct error) — no misleading 409 Conflict + 404 body mismatch.
  • Verify edit of sublocations as well (the user reports both edit and delete failing) — see updateSublocation.go.
  • Detail / markers / geodata Redis caches invalidated after a successful delete (the Go action already does this — confirm it runs).

QA Summary 23/07/2026

Result

PASSED with data-state caveat. Current Go API can create, edit, and delete sublocations for real photographer data. The originally reported sublocation 36 is no longer present under gothru_user_id=253 / clever-click, so requests against 36 now correctly return 404 sublocation not found. No tested endpoint returned HTTP 500.

LinkedIn Login

Initiates the OAuth2 flow by generating a secure state and redirecting to LinkedIn.

Method: GET

Example Usage

Handles the redirect from LinkedIn after user authorization. This endpoint verifies the security state and exchanges the authorization code for user data.

Method: GET
Auth Required: No (Verified via linkedin_oauth_state cookie)

  • state (string): The security state string returned by LinkedIn.

  "requestTime": 150,

Overview

Migrate the linkedin_auth session cookie value from the internal database primary key (id as an integer) to the unique LinkedIn identifier (linkedin_id as a string, the OIDC sub claim). This ensures consistent user identification across sessions and simplifies lookup logic.

    Expires:  time.Now().Add(24 * time.Hour),
    HTTPOnly: true,
    Secure:   true,
    SameSite: "Lax",
})

func GetLinkedInUserByLinkedinID(linkedinID string) (*models.Linkedin, error) {
    db := config.GetConnPhotographers()

RESULT 19/06/26

✅ Implementation Complete — Ready for Unit Testing

Summary

The GET /v1/photographers/{gothruUserId}/location endpoint returns a stale list of sublocations. A photographer can have up to 4 sublocations, but the endpoint keeps returning the previous cached value (e.g. 3) after a new sublocation is added.

Root cause

This is a cache invalidation bug, not a data-retrieval bug.

  • The location controller caches the response under photographer:v*:location:<gothruUserId> (helpers.RedisKey.PhotographerLocation).
  • When a sublocation is added (AddSublocation) or updated (UpdateSublocation), the cache invalidation cleared the detail, geodata, count, and markers patterns — but not the location pattern (PhotographerLocationPattern).
  • Result: the detail endpoint reflects 4 sublocations, while the location endpoint keeps serving the stale cached value (3) until the TTL expires.

The invalidation pattern (PhotographerLocationPattern, photographer:v*:location:<id>) already exists in helpers/redis_keys.go; it was simply never invoked from the sublocation mutations.

Fix

Add PhotographerLocationPattern invalidation, keyed by photographer.GothruUserID (the location cache is keyed by gothru user id only), in both mutation actions:

  • src/action/v1/sublocations/addSublocation.go
  • src/action/v1/sublocations/updateSublocation.go
_, _ = helpers.ClearRedisKeys(helpers.RedisKey.PhotographerLocationPattern(photographer.GothruUserID))

The v* wildcard in the pattern covers all cache versions.

GetPhotographerLocation (action + controller) needs no change — its query is correct (Find with no limit, no soft-delete on the model).

Verification

  • go build ./src/action/v1/sublocations/ passes.
  • Manual: add a 4th sublocation, then call the location endpoint — it now returns 4 immediately instead of the stale 3.

Out of scope (noted, not changed)

The DB column is misspelled latilatitude (mapped in models/directory_photographer_sublocation.go and referenced by raw SQL in getBulkCityPhotographerCounts.go and getPhotographerCount.go). Renaming it requires a DB migration plus updating all references; left as-is to avoid breaking production queries.

Objective:
Modify the GetPhotographersDashboard API to prioritize photographers with a "pending" status ( status = 1 ) by placing them at the top of the returned results.

Changes Implemented:

  • Updated the GORM query's Order clause in src/action/v1/photographers/getPhotographersDashboard.go .
  • Replaced the simple chronological sort ( created_at DESC ) with a conditional SQL CASE statement.
  • The new sorting logic: CASE WHEN status = 1 THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, created_at DESC .
    • Primary Sort: Evaluates the status field. Records with status = 1 are assigned a lower sorting weight ( 0 ), forcing them to the top of the query result. All other statuses are assigned a higher weight ( 1 ).
    • Secondary Sort: Falls back to sorting by created_at DESC , ensuring that within the "pending" group (and the subsequent non-pending group), the newest entries still appear first.
  • This approach is chosen because it is cross-compatible across different SQL database engines (such as PostgreSQL and MySQL) without breaking the existing pagination implementation ( Limit and Offset ).

Photographer Dashboard Pending First

Date: 2026-06-24

Request: Update /v1/photographers/users/dashboard so pending photographer
accounts appear first in the dashboard list.

1. Background

The Featured Photographers dashboard is used by support/admin users to review
photographer accounts and take action on their status.

Today, accounts waiting for review can be buried across many pages. This creates
extra manual work because the reviewer must scan page after page to find the
accounts that need attention.

The screenshot feedback is clear: pending accounts should be visible first
because they are the work queue.

2. User Problem

Support users need to review pending photographer accounts quickly.

They do not have time to go through many pages of denied, approved, or older
accounts just to find the accounts that are still waiting for action.

When pending accounts are hidden deeper in the list:

  • Reviews take longer.
  • Pending accounts may be missed.
  • Account approval or denial is delayed.
  • The dashboard feels harder to use than it needs to be.

3. Desired Experience

When the photographer dashboard opens, pending accounts should appear at the top
of the list by default.

After pending accounts are shown, the rest of the list can continue in the
normal order, with the newest accounts first.

The dashboard should still feel familiar. This is not a redesign. It is a better
default order that matches the reviewer's priority.

4. Recommended Product Direction

Use Pending first as the default dashboard order.

This means:

  • Pending photographers appear before denied, approved, and featured
    photographers.
  • Within the pending group, the newest pending accounts appear first.
  • After pending accounts, other accounts continue in newest-first order.
  • Existing search behavior remains the same.
  • Existing status filter behavior remains the same.
  • No new button or training is required.

This is the simplest change that directly solves the user pain.

5. Alternatives Considered

Option A - Keep Current Order

This keeps the dashboard unchanged, but it does not solve the problem. Support
still has to search through multiple pages to find pending accounts.

Option B - Add a Manual Pending Filter

This helps, but it still requires the reviewer to remember to use the filter.
The problem is urgent enough that the dashboard should show pending accounts
first automatically.

Option C - Create a Separate Pending Review Queue

This could be useful in the future, especially if the review process becomes
larger. For now, it is more than needed. The current dashboard can solve the
main problem by showing pending accounts first.

Recommended Option

The existing filter can remain available, but the default view should keep the
familiar dashboard layout with one important change: pending accounts are
prioritized first.

6. Success Criteria

The change is successful when:

  • A reviewer can open the dashboard and immediately see pending accounts on the
    first page when pending accounts exist.
  • Reviewers no longer need to scan many pages to find pending accounts.
  • Search and status filters continue to work as users expect.
  • The dashboard still feels like the same dashboard, only easier to review.

7. Out of Scope

This brainstorm does not require:

  • A full dashboard redesign.
  • A new review workflow.
  • New status labels.
  • New buttons or navigation.
  • Changes to how reviewers approve, deny, or log in as photographers.

8. Plain-Language Acceptance Criteria

  • When pending accounts exist, they show before non-pending accounts.
  • Pending accounts are ordered with the newest pending accounts first.
  • Non-pending accounts still appear after pending accounts.
  • If the user searches, the results still match the search.
  • If the user selects a status filter, the dashboard still respects that filter.
  • The reviewer can find pending accounts without going through many pages.

issues.display_title: Issue #38: Fix: Create Portfolio 500 "invalid character 'ï'" on Gothru/ Tourmkr Thumbnail Fetch (BOM)
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 02/07/26

✅ Implementation: Portfolio Thumbnail Fetch BOM Fix

Overview

This document outlines the root cause and the implemented solution for the issue where creating a portfolio item (Gothru/Tourmkr) resulted in a 500 Internal Server Error due to a UTF-8 Byte Order Mark (BOM) in the upstream API response.

Task Reference

Project Board: Photographer API GO (Project 104)
Task Title: Fix: Create Portfolio 500 "invalid character 'A_'" on Gothru/ Tourmkr Thumbnail Fetch (BOM)

1. The Problem

When users attempted to create a portfolio item using a tourmkr.com value (type: 3), the system triggered a fetch for a thumbnail via resolveThumbnailForType. This internally calls the upstream API (https://apil.gothru.co/virtualtours/public/first-pano).

The upstream API occasionally returned JSON prefixed with a UTF-8 Byte Order Mark (BOM: EF BB BF). Because encoding/json in Go's standard library does not handle BOMs implicitly when parsing JSON, the json.NewDecoder().Decode() execution failed with the error:
invalid character 'A_' looking for beginning of value

This error propagated up to the main handler, failing the entire portfolio creation process with a 500 Internal Server Error, even though the thumbnail is an optional field.

2. Implementation Details

The fix was implemented in two distinct layers to ensure resilience:

Part 1: Stripping the BOM Before JSON Parsing

In src/action/v1/portfolio/portfolioHelper.go (specifically in the FetchGothruFirstPano function), we replaced json.NewDecoder(...).Decode(...) with an approach that reads the bytes first, strips any BOM if present, and then unmarshals the clean payload.

// Read response bytes
bodyBytes, _ := io.ReadAll(apiRes.Body)

// Trim UTF-8 BOM
bodyBytes = bytes.TrimPrefix(bodyBytes, []byte{0xEF, 0xBB, 0xBF})

// Unmarshal safely
if err := json.Unmarshal(bodyBytes, &result); err != nil {
    return "", 0, err
}

This was applied to both the success path (HTTP 200) and the non-200 error-checking path (to safely extract the upstream message).

Part 2: Graceful Degradation for Thumbnail Failures

In src/action/v1/portfolio/createPhotographerPortfolio.go, the portfolio creation logic was refactored so that a failure in resolving the thumbnail does not abort the entire portfolio creation request.

Instead of propagating the error from resolveThumbnailForType, the system now catches it, logs a warning, and gracefully continues with an empty thumbnail pointer:

// Resolve thumbnail URL
thumbUrl, err := resolveThumbnailForType(pType, value)
if err != nil {
	fmt.Printf("Warning: failed to resolve thumbnail: %v\n", err)
	thumbUrl = ""
}

3. Acceptance Criteria Met

  • POST to /v1/photographers/{userId}/portfolio with type: 3 and a valid tourmkr URL succeeds (201 Created) even when the upstream first-pano API responds with a BOM-prefixed JSON.
  • Upstream JSON is now parsed BOM-tolerantly at both decode sites inside FetchGothruFirstPano.
  • A failure in thumbnail resolution no longer results in a 500 error; the system degrades gracefully and creates the portfolio item without a thumbnail.
  • All existing validation layers (type, title, duplicate tour keys) remain intact and fully functional.

Report

Creating a portfolio item fails with a 500 for (potentially) all users:

Request — POST {{base_url}}/v1/photographers/{{gothruUserId}}/portfolio

{ "type": 3, "title": "Bhopal", "value": "https://tourmkr.com/F1aK5Z1AR5" }

user_id: 19311

Response

{ "statusCode": 500, "requestTime": 31, "data": { "error": "invalid character 'ï' looking for beginning of value" } }

Root cause (confirmed in code)

invalid character 'ï' looking for beginning of value is the classic Go symptom of a UTF-8 BOM (EF BB BF → ï»¿) at the start of a JSON body that encoding/json is asked to decode.

For type: 3 (gothru) with a tourmkr.com value, portfolio creation resolves a thumbnail:

  • CreatePhotographerPortfolio → resolveThumbnailForType(pType, value) (src/action/v1/portfolio/createPhotographerPortfolio.go:78)
  • → FetchGothruFirstPano(tourkey, userId) calls the external API and decodes its response (src/action/v1/portfolio/portfolioHelper.go:337-365): 
    apiRes, _ := http.Get("https://apil.gothru.co/virtualtours/public/first-pano?tour_key=%s&user_id=%d")
...
if err := json.NewDecoder(apiRes.Body).Decode(&result); err != nil {
    return "", 0, err   // <- BOM in response body -> "invalid character 'ï' ..."
}

The upstream apil.gothru.co/virtualtours/public/first-pano response is BOM-prefixed (or otherwise non-clean JSON). json.Decode does not strip a BOM, so it errors; that error propagates up (resolveThumbnailForType → CreatePhotographerPortfolio → mapPortfolioError) and the entire create returns 500 — even though the thumbnail is optional. The same json.Unmarshal on the non-200 branch (portfolioHelper.go:349) has the same weakness.

Fix (two parts)

  1. Strip the BOM before decoding the upstream response:

    body, _ := io.ReadAll(apiRes.Body)
body = bytes.TrimPrefix(body, []byte{0xEF, 0xBB, 0xBF})
json.Unmarshal(body, &result)

    Apply to both decode sites in FetchGothruFirstPano (lines ~349 and ~363).

  2. Don't 500 the whole create on a thumbnail failure. Thumbnail is optional (thumbPtr may be nil). If resolveThumbnailForType fails, log and continue creating the portfolio with an empty thumbnail rather than aborting (createPhotographerPortfolio.go:78-81).

Acceptance criteria

  • POST …/portfolio with type:3 + a valid tourmkr URL succeeds (201) even when the first-pano API returns a BOM-prefixed body.
  • Upstream JSON is parsed BOM-tolerantly at both decode sites in FetchGothruFirstPano.
  • A thumbnail-resolution failure degrades to "no thumbnail" instead of a 500 (portfolio item still created).
  • Verified with the reported case (user 19311, https://tourmkr.com/F1aK5Z1AR5).
  • Existing validation (type/title/value, duplicate tour key) unchanged.

The upstream first-pano endpoint still returns a BOM-prefixed JSON body for the reported tour, but the backend no longer fails with invalid character 'Ã¯' looking for beginning of value. 	deletes := []struct {

Result: pass.

Description

Administrative workflow & data-management enhancement for 360photographers.org, for data compliance and to keep the admin dashboard clean.

Account Deletion Sync: Currently, if a user deletes their main GoThru account, their profile remains orphaned in the 360 Photographers Directory. Implement a cascading deletion / synchronization mechanism so that deleting a GoThru account automatically removes the user's profile (and associated data) from the directory.

Acceptance Criteria

  1. When a user deletes their GoThru account, their profile and associated data are automatically and completely removed from 360photographers.org.

Technical notes (grounded in this repo)

  • Cross-database join, no FK cascade possible. The GoThru account lives in users (ConnGothruMod); the directory profile lives in photographers (ConnPhotographers) — a different database — joined by photographers.gothru_user_id = users.user_id. A DB-level ON DELETE CASCADE can't span the two connections, so this needs an application-level sync:
    • Option A — event/webhook: the GoThru account-deletion flow notifies this service (or publishes to RabbitMQ) → a consumer deletes the directory profile.
    • Option B — endpoint: expose an internal DELETE /v1/photographers/:gothruUserId that the GoThru side calls on account deletion.
    • Option C — reconciliation job: periodic sweep removing directory profiles whose gothru_user_id no longer exists in users.
  • "Associated data" to remove (all keyed by the photographer row, ConnPhotographers): photographers, photographer_sublocations, portfolios, equipment, service links, availability links, reviews, and slug history. Wrap in a transaction.
  • Cache + search invalidation: clear detail / list / dashboard / markers / geodata / count Redis patterns and any Martin/tile or search-index entries so the removed profile disappears from the map and directory immediately.
  • No whole-profile delete endpoint exists today (only sub-resource deletes: equipment/portfolio/services/availability), so this is net-new.

Extended acceptance criteria (proposed)

  • Deleting a GoThru account removes the directory profile and all associated rows (sublocations, portfolio, equipment, services, availabilities, reviews, slug history).
  • Sync mechanism agreed (event/webhook vs endpoint vs reconciliation) and documented, since it spans two databases.
  • Relevant Redis caches + map/search entries invalidated so the profile no longer appears.
  • Idempotent + safe if the profile was already removed / never existed.

Note — second enhancement not captured here. The source feedback mentions two items: this account-deletion sync and "I need to be able to delete requests, since I do not want to be stuck with rejected requests forever." That request-deletion capability is a separate piece of work and is not covered by this issue. Recommend a separate task for it — say the word and I'll create it.

Summary

Add two new columns to the photographers table:

  • is_deleted — support-only flag to hide a photographer from the support dashboard list (GET /v1/photographers/users/dashboard). Public endpoints are NOT affected.
  • request_date — set whenever the photographer notifies support of a profile update (NotifyPhotographerUpdate).

RESULT 22/07/26

✅ Implementation Report: Issue #46 Ranking Recompute + V2 Cache Invalidation

Issue: #46

PR: #48

Summary

Implemented the follow-up fix for stale v2 photographer directory ordering.

The issue had two related problems:

  • Service and sublocation writes changed fields that affect ranking, but did not recompute the stored photographers.ranking` value.
  • Several scored write paths could leave GET /v2/photographers/users serving stale cached ordering from PhotographerListV2.

Review Update

PR review found a race in the first implementation:

clear V2 cache -> async RecomputeAndSaveRanking -> DB ranking update

A request between the cache clear and the ranking update could rebuild the v2 list cache using the old ranking, then keep that stale cache for up to 24 hours.

The implementation was updated so RecomputeAndSaveRanking clears PhotographerListV2 only after the ranking update succeeds. This makes the cache invalidation happen at the true source of ranking changes and covers all current ranking recompute callers, including the ranking backfill flow.

  • src/action/v1/services/addPhotographerServices.go

  • src/action/v1/sublocations/removeSublocation.go
  • src/action/v1/sublocations/updateSublocation.go

Central V2 Cache Invalidation

RecomputeAndSaveRanking now clears the v2 photographer list cache after persisting the new ranking:

if err := config.GetConnPhotographers().Model(&p).Update("ranking", ranking).Error; err == nil { //nolint
	_, _ = helpers.ClearRedisKeys(helpers.RedisKey.PhotographerListV2Pattern())
}

This prevents the stale-cache race and avoids duplicating v2 list invalidation across every write path that recomputes ranking.

RESULT 22/07/26

✅ Implementation Report: Issue #47 Global Average Rating API

Issue: #47

Branch: feat/issue-47-rating-summary

Summary

Implemented a backend endpoint for the directory-wide average photographer rating.

The frontend currently uses a hardcoded average rating stat. This task adds a real API source for that value, backed by the reviews table and cached in Redis.

Endpoint

GET /v1/photographers/rating-summary

Example API Hit

curl -X GET "http://localhost:3000/v1/photographers/rating-summary" \
  -H "Accept: application/json"

With cache bypass:

curl -X GET "http://localhost:3000/v1/photographers/rating-summary?disablecache=true" \
  -H "Accept: application/json"

Example Response

{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "requestTime": 12,
  "data": {
    "avgRating": 4.8,
    "totalReviews": 123
  }
}

When no visible rated reviews exist:

{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "requestTime": 8,
  "data": {
    "avgRating": 0,
    "totalReviews": 0
  }
}

Source Of Truth

The endpoint calculates:

SELECT ROUND(AVG(rating), 1) AS avg_rating, COUNT(*) AS total_reviews
FROM reviews
WHERE rating IS NOT NULL AND status IN (2, 3);

Reason:

  • reviews.rating is the per-review source of truth.
  • Existing public review listing uses status IN (2, 3) in src/action/v1/reviews/getReviews.go, so the rating summary follows the same visible-review definition.
  • Averaging reviews weights each review equally. It avoids averaging photographers.rating_avg, which would weight each photographer equally regardless of review count.
